title: KCET 2014 Physics

questions.q: A microscope is having objective of focal length 1 cm and eyepiece of focal length 6 cm. If tube length is 30 cm and image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision, what is the magnification produced by the microscope? Take D = 25 cm.
questions.explanation: Using M = (L/f_o)(D/f_e) = (30/1)(25/6) = 125; using the more exact M = (L/f_o)(1+D/f_e) gives ~155, close to 150 — this ambiguity between the two commonly taught formulas is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.q: A fringe width of a certain interference pattern is $\beta$ = 0.002 cm. What is the distance of 5$^{th}$ dark fringe from centre?
questions.explanation: Using y = n$\beta$ = 5 \times 0.002 = 0.01 cm = 1\times10^{-2} cm (option 3); the stricter formula y=(n-1/2)$\beta$ gives 0.009 cm — this ambiguity is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.q: Which of the following spectral series of hydrogen atom is lying in visible range of electromagnetic wave?
questions.explanation: The Balmer series (transitions to n=2) lies in the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: In n type semiconductor, electrons are majority charge carriers but it does not show any negative charge. The reason is
options: mobility of electrons is extremely small
questions.explanation: The donor atoms remain electrically neutral (equal protons and electrons) even after donating a free electron, so the crystal as a whole stays neutral.

questions.q: For the given digital circuit, write the truth table and identify the logic gate it represents: [Two NOR gates, each with both inputs tied to A and B respectively, feed into a third NOR gate whose output is Y]
questions.explanation: Each first-stage NOR gate (inputs A,A and B,B) acts as a NOT gate, giving A' and B'; NOR-ing A' and B' gives Y = (A'+B')' = AB, i.e. an AND gate.

Two equal and opposite charges of masses m$_1$ and m$_2$ are accelerated in a uniform electric field through the same distance. What is the ratio of their accelerations if their ratio of masses is \dfrac{m$_1$}{m$_2$} = 0.5?
questions.explanation: Since a = qE/m and the charges have equal magnitude, a$_1$/a$_2$ = m$_2$/m$_1$ = 1/0.5 = 2.

questions.q: What is the nature of Gaussian surface involved in Gauss law of electrostatic?
questions.explanation: A Gaussian surface is an imaginary closed surface; the flux through it is a scalar quantity, so it is best described as a scalar/imaginary construct — the ambiguity of this wording is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.explanation: Green=5, Black=0, Violet=$10^7$, Gold=$\pm$5%; value = 50\times10^7 $\Omega$ = 500 M$\Omega$ $\pm$5%.

questions.q: Two resistors of resistances 2 $\Omega$ and 6 $\Omega$ are connected in parallel. This combination is then connected to a battery of emf 2V and internal resistance 0.5 $\Omega$. What is the current flowing through the battery?

In a potentiometer experiment of a cell of emf 1.25 V gives balancing length of 30 cm. If the cell is replaced by another cell, balancing length is found to be 40 cm. What is the emf of second cell?
questions.explanation: EMFs are proportional to balancing lengths: E$_2$ = 1.25 \times (40/30) $\approx$ 1.67 V.

questions.q: A charged particle experiences magnetic force in the presence of magnetic field. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: The particle is moving and magnetic field is parallel to velocity.
The particle is stationary and magnetic field is parallel.
The particle is moving and magnetic field is perpendicular to the velocity.
The particle is stationary and magnetic field is perpendicular.
questions.explanation: Magnetic force F = qv \times B is maximum (non-zero) when the particle moves with velocity perpendicular to B; a stationary charge feels no magnetic force.

questions.q: If a velocity has both perpendicular and parallel components while moving through a magnetic field, what is the path followed by a charged particle?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular component causes circular motion while the parallel component gives uniform motion along the field, combining to give a helical path.

questions.q: A solenoid has length 0.4 cm, radius 1 cm and 400 turns of wire. If a current of 5 A is passed through this solenoid, what is the magnetic field inside the solenoid?
questions.explanation: B = $\mu_0$nI with n = N/l; taking the printed length (0.4 cm) literally gives an unrealistically huge field, so the intended length was likely 0.4 m — this inconsistency is probably why KEA awarded a grace mark. With l = 0.4 m, n = 1000/m and B = 4$\pi$\times10^{-7}\times1000\times5 $\approx$ 6.28\times10^{-3} T (option 1).

questions.q: A gyromagnetic ratio of the electron revolving in a circular orbit of hydrogen atom is 8.8 \times 10^{10} C kg$^{-1}$. What is the mass of the electron? Given charge of the electron = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} C.
questions.explanation: Gyromagnetic ratio = e/(2m), so m = e/(2\times ratio) = 1.6\times10^{-19}/(2\times8.8\times10^{10}) = \dfrac{1}{11}\times10^{-29} kg.

questions.explanation: A large positive susceptibility (of the order of hundreds/thousands) is characteristic of ferromagnetic materials.

A multimeter reads a voltage of a certain A.C. source as 100 V. What is the peak value of voltage of A.C. source?
questions.explanation: Multimeters read rms values; V$_0$ = V$_{rms}$\times\sqrt{2} = 100\times1.414 = 141.4 V.

questions.q: A series LCR circuit contains inductance 5 mH, capacitance 2 $\mu$F and resistance 10 $\Omega$. If a frequency A.C. source is varied, what is the frequency at which maximum power is dissipated?
questions.explanation: Maximum power occurs at resonance: f = 1/(2$\pi\sqrt{LC}$) = 1/(2$\pi\sqrt{5\times10^{-3}\times2\times10^{-6}}$) = 1/(2$\pi\times10^{-4}$) = (5/$\pi$)\times10^3 Hz.

A body starts from rest and moves with constant acceleration for t s. It travels a distance x$_1$ in first half of time and x$_2$ in next half of time, then
questions.explanation: x$_1$ = \dfrac{1}{2}a(t/2)^2 = at^2/8; total distance in t is at^2/2, so x$_2$ = at^2/2 - at^2/8 = 3at^2/8 = 3x$_1$.

questions.q: A person is driving a vehicle at uniform speed of 5 ms$^{-1}$ on a level curved track of radius 5 m. The coefficient of static friction between tyres and road is 0.1. Will the person slip while taking the turn with the same speed? Take g = 10 ms$^{-2}$. Choose the correct statement.
options: A person will slip if v$^2$ > 5 ms$^{-1}$
A person will not slip if v$^2$ > 10 ms$^{-1}$
A person will slip if v$^2$ = 5 ms$^{-1}$
A person will slip if v$^2$ < 5 ms$^{-1}$
questions.explanation: Maximum safe speed satisfies v$^2$ = $\mu$gr = 0.1\times10\times5 = 5; the person slips if v$^2$ exceeds this value (here v$^2$=25>5, so slips).

questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: $\vec\tau = \vec r \times \vec F$ = (1,-2,1)\times(5,2,-5) = (8, 10, 12), i.e. $8\hat i+10\hat j+12\hat k$.

A period of geostationary satellite is

questions.q: A flow of liquid is streamline if the Reynold number is
questions.explanation: Flow is streamline (laminar) for Reynolds number less than about 1000.

questions.q: A pipe of 30 cm long and open at both the ends produces harmonics. Which harmonic mode of pipe resonates a 1.1 kHz source? Given speed of sound in air = 330 ms$^{-1}$.
questions.explanation: Fundamental frequency f$_1$ = v/2L = 330/0.6 = 550 Hz; 1100 Hz = 2\times550 Hz, i.e. the second harmonic (all harmonics allowed in an open pipe).

questions.q: In anomalous expansion of water, at what temperature, the density of water is maximum?
questions.explanation: Water has its maximum density at 4 $^{\circ}$C due to anomalous expansion.

questions.q: A cycle tyre bursts suddenly. What is the type of this process?
questions.explanation: A sudden burst happens too fast for heat exchange with surroundings, so it is an adiabatic process.

questions.q: An object is placed at 20 cm in front of a concave mirror produces three times magnified real image. What is focal length of the concave mirror?
questions.explanation: For a real, magnified image, m = -v/u = -3 (with u=-20), giving v=-60 cm; using mirror formula, 1/f = 1/v+1/u = -1/60-1/20 = -1/15, so f = 15 cm.
